items.title: Eating disorders are on the rise. GLP-1s could make things worse.
items.raw_text: GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are one of the biggest biotech breakthroughs of the last decade. But to some clinical psychologists, they can represent something more sinister—a potential trigger for eating disorders. A new report suggests that the global incidence of anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa shot up between 1990 and 2023—by a whopping 71%. By 2023, there were an estimated 18.1 million people living with one of these two disorders. What’s worse is that the number is likely to be much higher than that once we factor in other eating disorders. And, disturbingly, those in the field are already starting to see GLP-1 weight-loss drugs exacerbating the issue. Cheri Levinson is a clinical psychologist at the University of Louisville in Kentucky who has specialized in eating disorders for almost 20 years. She says she’s now seeing more patients with more severe symptoms than at any other time in her career, and that many of them are misusing GLP-1s. “This is the worst I’ve seen things,” she says. Eating disorders are mental health conditions in which people’s eating behaviors impact their health. They include anorexia nervosa (defined by a fear of weight gain), bulimia nervosa (in which people binge and purge), binge eating disorder, and others. items.raw_text: How I Built the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World Don't be put off by the clickbait headline, this piece by Jacob Sansbury describing how they are building Spawn is a fascinating exploration of the bleeding edge of what's possible with agentic engineering against frontier models. Spawn is a massively multiplayer gaming environment where players can use prompts (to the in-game agent, Savi) to modify the game world. I fired it up on my phone for a few minutes and was able to prompt a castle into existence, then a dragon, then ride the dragon to fly around that castle. By Jacob's telling, Spawn is now being developed autonomously by a swarm of Fable-powered agents costing over $3 million in tokens per month ("we spend 30x payroll on AI tokens"). Our agents change the live code directly and ship to production hourly, so they read every error, bug report and metric themselves. About 60% of our work starts from a production error, a Savi bug report (Savi is the AI you build games with in Spawn), something odd in our logs, or a feature request. Savi files bugs herself. When a user hits one, or Savi hits one in the product, she files it. It goes straight to an agent that decides whether it's a real bug to fix, something we won't fix, or intentional design that needs a decision. Usually it becomes a change, delivered to that user within an hour, with a message in the same chat. items.raw_text: De nieuwe centrale bibliotheek van Essen in Duitsland opende op zaterdag 24 oktober 2026 haar deuren, met een interieur ontworpen door MVRDV en includi, in samenwerking met Meyer Architekten. Door de verhuizing naar een centrale locatie in de stad kon de verbinding tussen de bibliotheek en bezoekers opnieuw worden vormgegeven. Het gerenoveerde interieur van 10.000 m² in een voormalig winkelpand telt zes verdiepingen. De nieuwe Zentralbibliothek is opgezet als ‘derde plek’ – een toegankelijke locatie voor de inwoners van Essen. Boekenkasten en een actieve binnengevel vormen de bouwstenen van het interieur. Deze verhuizing van de bibliotheek is een belangrijk project voor de stad Essen. Van de voormalige locatie naast het station verhuist de bibliotheek naar het vroegere Boeckerhaus, een bekend warenhuis in het stadshart. Het Boeckerhaus heeft van oudsher een sterke band met boeken: tot 2017 was hier boekhandel Mayersche gevestigd. Met deze transformatie krijgt het gebouw een nieuwe functie als levendige plek voor cultuur en onderwijs in de binnenstad. Voor dit ontwerp hebben de samenwerkende bureaus gekeken naar de geschiedenis en ontwikkeling van bibliotheken door de eeuwen heen. Ooit waren bibliotheken monumentale plekken alleen toegankelijk voor de elite en later werden het openbare plekken voor een breed publiek. From ALA: The Association of College and Research Libraries (ACRL) announces the publication of “ Open Movements: Recognizing Challenges and Building Connections ,” edited by Abbey K. Elder, Shannon M. Smith, and Bryan Ricupero. This collection surfaces the work taking place across open movements and highlights how practitioners and advocates can effectively collaborate for sustainable change. Open movements all center public access and broad representation, and work to prevent the concentration of power governing information and its monetization. As general discussion of openness has narrowed to focus on areas like open science, data, access, and education, these individual communities have grown distanced from each other and, occasionally, their shared values. In five sections, “Open Movements: Recognizing Challenges and Building Connections” explores different perspectives on open and how the values that guide open systems and practices will remain relevant well into the future. items.raw_text: Rijksmuseum Meermanno (Voorheen Huis van het Boek) heeft het naastgelegen pand aan de Prinsessegracht 32 in Den Haag verworven. Hiermee voegt het boekenmuseum driehonderd vierkante meter toe aan zijn vloeroppervlak. In aanloop naar het 175-jarig jubileum in 2027 werkt het museum aan een vernieuwingsplan. Deze uitbreiding is daar onderdeel van. Rijksmuseum Meermanno beheert een nationale erfgoedcollectie van zo’n 500.000 objecten, waaronder 90.000 historische boeken, vroege drukken en zeldzame middeleeuwse handschriften. De aankoop van Prinsessegracht 32 maakt de komst van een nieuw studiecentrum met een inpandig depot mogelijk. Het middelpunt van deze uitbreiding moet de Leeskamer worden, een plek waar onderzoekers, studenten en bezoekers in directe verbinding staan met het depot. Behoud collectie De aanleiding voor de uitbreiding is tweeledig. Allereerst is er een dringende noodzaak rondom het behoud van de collectie. Een groot deel ligt nu nog opgeslagen in de depots op het terrein van de KB in Den Haag. Dit terrein wordt in de komende jaren herontwikkeld en daarmee vervalt de externe depotruimte van het museum. Daarnaast loopt het museum in de huidige panden tegen zijn fysieke grenzen aan, met een tekort aan ruimte voor educatie en publieksfuncties. De aankoop is mede mogelijk gemaakt door steun van het ministerie van Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap, gemeente Den Haag en Stichting Vrienden Rijksmuseum Meermanno. Microsoft fixes a Windows 11 annoyance as PC revenue declines
items.raw_text: Microsoft is beginning the rollout of a Windows 11 preview update that finally addresses a persistent power user complaint with the operating system: the right-click menu that obliterated years of muscle memory on command locations and hid others behind an additional click. The timing is notable, as the announcement comes alongside Microsoft's quarterly financial report, which showed a continued decline in the business of selling Windows licenses for new PCs. The preview update, KB5127936 , is cumulative for Windows 11 versions 26H2 and 25H2. The update will be a gradual rollout before eventually moving on to a normal rollout for all Windows 11 devices once it reaches general availability. The highlight of the new update should calm annoyed users who have spent years with custom scripts and services in an attempt to shape Windows the way they would prefer it. Users will get a "customize menu" button that controls what commands appear when they right-click their mouse. Users can toggle built-in commands such as Send To or Create Shortcut on or off, rearrange what appears on the main menu, and control which third-party extensions show up in either the main or submenus. The gripe with the right-click menu had been that Microsoft hid familiar command locations behind a top row of icons while moving other familiar commands under the "Show more options" submenu. Now, Windows users can customize the whole thing around their habits. The original Windows 11 right-click menu is a mess.

items.title: Pentagon IG refuses to investigate Starlink/Starshield slowdown in Ukraine
items.raw_text: The Pentagon inspector general's office declined a request from US senators to investigate restrictions recently imposed on the Ukraine military's use of SpaceX's satellite network. Ukraine, which uses SpaceX's Starlink service and the military version known as Starshield, said earlier this month that military drones lost satellite connectivity when traveling above 161 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour). The limit was removed after about 10 days. Five Democratic and four Republican senators sent an October 15 letter to Department of Defense Inspector General Platte Moring, asking for a probe into the reported disruptions of Starlink and Starshield. The letter asked, among other things, "whether any restrictions on Starlink or Starshield services were directed, authorized, or implemented by SpaceX, the Department of Defense, or other US government entities; whether such restrictions were consistent with applicable US government contracts, and what actions, if any, the Department of Defense took in response." items.title: Trump declares robot imports a national security threat
items.raw_text: President Donald Trump has declared the imports of foreign-made factory robots to be a national security threat—ordering new US negotiations with trading partners while holding out the possibility of imposing new tariffs on such robot imports in the future. Issued on October 28, Trump’s presidential proclamation represents heightened government scrutiny of foreign-made industrial robots that could complicate the manufacturing operations of major US corporations that rely on such robots. Those companies include Detroit automakers General Motors and Ford, electric vehicle manufacturer Tesla , and aerospace and defense giants like Boeing and Lockheed Martin. Trump’s proclamation describes industrial robots and machinery as being crucial for producing US military weapon systems along with representing a “driving force” behind all critical infrastructure sectors within the US economy. The proclamation cites an investigation under US Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick as having found that US imports of such robots “pose[] risks to the United States industrial base and threatens the long-term competitiveness of the United States in a sector that is increasingly vital to national security.” Read full article Comments

items.title: Trump ignored intel on China’s Nvidia spy to protect company’s stock, report says
items.raw_text: Donald Trump apparently is so aligned with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang—who has become the president’s key advisor on AI —that he ignored intelligence indicating that Huang was the target of a “Chinese spy plot,” and did so partly to protect Nvidia’s stock. The New York Times spoke with people briefed on US intelligence agencies’ surveillance and granted them anonymity to discuss findings drawn from “classified intelligence.” According to sources, about a year ago, Trump was briefed that “Beijing was getting reports from someone with direct access” to Huang. That “someone” was Alice Huang, or Huang Le, a Chinese citizen and former top executive at a Singapore cloud company called Megaspeed. According to sources, the US had already suspected that Alice Huang—who is not related to Jensen Huang—was helping China evade export controls to gain access to high-end Nvidia chips through Megaspeed. But it alarmed investigators to discover that she may have used her role at Megaspeed to gain direct access to Jensen Huang. It’s now believed she may have leveraged that closeness to feed China intel not only on one of America’s leading AI companies, but also to influence Trump’s thinking on AI. As Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted last month ahead of Trump’s AI talks with China President Xi Jinping, “the president is completely aligned with Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia.” Read full article Comments

items.title: Turning a solar power system into its own backup
items.raw_text: Rather than directly converting photons into electricity, concentrated solar energy uses mirrors to turn sunlight into heat, which can then be used to drive traditional generating turbines. Up to about a decade ago, there was a case to be made that concentrated solar energy had a bright future, as improvements in heat storage had turned it into a way to generate power around the clock. It wasn't to be. While concentrated solar costs fell enough to compete with nuclear power, the price of photovoltaics plunged, making solar panels the cheapest source of power in most locations. Currently, if you have a good site to generate solar power, then the economics of PV panels are hard to beat. That has left us needing to build a mixture of other facilities—typically batteries and natural gas facilities—to handle overnight needs or weather-driven shortfalls. But a small company is promising that it can help avoid the need to build a separate facility. Its version of concentrated solar is designed so that a fossil-fueled backup system shares most of the generating hardware with the solar side. Read full article Comments

items.title: Google admits AI search makes less money, but it's fixing that with more ads
items.raw_text: Google parent Alphabet reported its Q3 financial results on Wednesday afternoon, showing a healthy rise in revenue for the months of July to September. But the company's stock price has taken a beating, marking one of the largest post-earnings drops in its history. It comes down to several troubling aspects of the new report, including an admission by the company that AI search isn't earning as much as organic search, and despite that, Google expects to spend even more on AI next year. The company took in almost $128 billion in Q3 2026, earning more than $26 billion in net income. These may sound like good numbers, but financial markets are not impressed. While revenue is up 25 percent versus last year, net income is almost $9 billion lower. As of this story's publication, the stock price is down almost 12 percent, and it was down about 13 percent earlier in the day. While revenue was up 25 percent year over year, analysts expected more. Google reported earnings per share of $2.12, but the consensus projection ahead of Wednesday was $3.02. Google's Cloud products actually beat expectations, crossing $30 billion in revenue. That's about a billion more than analyst guesses. Read full article Comments

items.title: Massive leak exposes 41,000 DHS workers and undercover ICE agents
items.raw_text: An unprecedented leak of Department of Homeland Security records has exposed details of more than 41,000 employees or contractors who work for the department and its constituent agencies. The records include email addresses, phone numbers, and office addresses, but also references to internal systems and sensitive information on undercover and surveillance programs. In all, the leak provides a map of how DHS is organized and how it operates. The records, which span DHS itself as well as seven component agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement and US Customs and Border Protection, were last updated on August 19, 2026. The transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets and cybersecurity researcher and journalist maia arson crimew previewed the data for WIRED, which they say they obtained from a group calling itself the Department of Peace. DDoSecrets published the archive, which it calls “Icepick,” on Wednesday. In a press release, DDoSecrets says the data is from DHS's Okta login system. In a note with the files, the hackers wrote, “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs.” Read full article Comments

Michel van Genderen, intensivist en projectleider bij het Erasmus MC, ziet AI als een mogelijkheid om dit te verbeteren. “We willen niet alleen de administratieve lasten voor zorgprofessionals verminderen, maar juist ook de informatievoorziening aan patiënten en hun familie verbeteren.” Thuis rustig nalezen De AI-app zorgt ervoor dat patiënten en familieleden niet uitsluitend op hun geheugen hoeven te vertrouwen.
